conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. I’ll be taking care of you tonight. Can you tell me what brought you to the hospital?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Hi… I’ve been vomiting since yesterday afternoon. I tried Ativan at home but it didn’t help. I just couldn’t stop.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. And how are you feeling now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Still nauseous. I feel shaky too. My blood sugar was 430 when I got here.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, your labs show high blood sugar and an acid imbalance, called ketoacidosis. We’re giving you insulin and fluids through your port to correct that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay… I’ve had this before. Is it bad this time?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s serious, but we’re treating it. Your anion gap was 28, which is high, but it’s already coming down with treatment.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my blood pressure? It’s always high when I’m sick like this.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it was 216 over 112 when you arrived, and your heart rate was fast. That’s why we admitted you to the ICU for close monitoring.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m sorry… I know I’ve been here a lot.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re here to help. Your history shows this is often linked to your gastroparesis and anxiety. We’re treating both.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your blood work shows your acid levels are improving. The insulin is working.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s good. I still feel sick to my stomach though.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re giving you Reglan and Zofran for nausea. You’re also getting IV fluids to stay hydrated.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your glucose is now 275, and your anion gap is down to 17. That’s a big improvement.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Morning… Is the vomiting from my diabetes or my stomach not emptying?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s likely both. Your gastroparesis means your stomach empties slowly, and when your sugars are high, it gets worse.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the anxiety? I know it makes it worse.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, anxiety can trigger or worsen nausea. Psychiatry reviewed your case and recommended switching from Ativan to Klonopin.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Why the change?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Klonopin may help with both anxiety and nausea long-term and has a lower risk of dependence. We’ll start it today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I’ll try it. I haven’t been great about seeing my psychiatrist, I know.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s okay. The important thing is you’re here now. We’ll help you set up follow-up before you go home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You did well overnight. You kept down a popsicle yesterday, and your nausea seems better.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I haven’t vomited since last night. That’s a relief.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Great. We’re going to try advancing your diet to clear liquids today, then maybe soft foods tomorrow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Can I eat regular food soon?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll take it step by step. If you tolerate the liquids, we’ll move forward. Your blood sugar needs to stay stable too.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: My sugars have been all over the place. I took my usual Lantus dose at home, but it didn’t help.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s common during flares. We gave you extra Humalog—35 units so far—and your sugars are improving.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll need to adjust my insulin at home too?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, you’ll continue your sliding scale with Humalog. We’ll make sure you have clear instructions before discharge.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your latest labs look good. Glucose is 130, and your electrolytes are balanced. The alkalosis has resolved.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. What about my blood pressure?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s still a bit high when you’re nauseous, but we switched you to captopril for now. You’ll go back to lisinopril at home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. I’m glad things are improving.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve done really well. You’re eating a regular diet now and haven’t vomited in over 24 hours.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I feel so much better. Can I go home today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’re planning to discharge you today. You’ll stop Ativan and start Klonopin twice a day.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And I need to see a psychiatrist?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, within a month, to continue the Klonopin. We also recommend following up with your diabetes team and PCP.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I don’t have a PCP right now… I was let go from my clinic.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. We’ll help you find a new provider. Your health is important, and we want to support you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I really want to do better.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We believe in you. Keep taking your medications, eat small meals, and reach out if nausea returns early.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. And if I feel anxious, I should take the Klonopin?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. It’s meant to help prevent the cycle of anxiety and vomiting. Don’t wait until you’re very sick.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That makes sense. Thank you for explaining everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. We’ll have your discharge papers ready soon, and a nurse will go over your meds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I’m ready to go home and take care of myself better.
